# `@ai-sdk/harness-claude-code`: last-step `finish-step` usage is the whole turn's cumulative total, not that step's own usage

Minimal reproduction. `npm install && npm run repro` — no API key needed, it
drives the package's own bridge event-processing code against a synthetic
(but protocol-accurate) Claude Code CLI stream.

## The bug

On any turn with **two or more model calls** (i.e. any turn with at least one
tool round trip before the final answer — subagents not required), the
`finish-step` part emitted for the **last** step reports the whole turn's
cumulative usage (every step summed) instead of that step's own usage.

Concretely, in [`packages/harness-claude-code/src/bridge/index.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/harness-claude-code/src/bridge/index.ts#L424-L457),
on the CLI's turn-ending `result` message:

```ts
const usage = msg.usage ?? msg.message?.usage; // cumulative, whole-turn total
const harnessUsage = mapUsage(usage);
if (harnessUsage) turnUsage = harnessUsage;
...
if (streamEventState.stepOpen) {
  emitFinishStep({
    state: streamEventState,
    emit,
    usage: harnessUsage ?? streamEventState.pendingStepUsage,
  });
}
```

`streamEventState.pendingStepUsage` is already sitting there with the right
value — the final step's own `assistant` message set it correctly (see
[`create-emit-stream-event.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/harness-claude-code/src/bridge/create-emit-stream-event.ts#L202-L247)).
But a text-only final response never runs through `closeStepIfReady()` (that
only fires from tool-result handling or `finishApprovalStep`), so the step is
still open when `result` arrives — and `harnessUsage` (the cumulative total)
wins over `pendingStepUsage` (the correct, final-step-only value) because of
the `??` precedence.

## Expected vs. actual

Given a turn with:
- step 1 (a Bash tool call): 1000 input / 50 output tokens
- step 2 (the final text answer): 1800 input / 70 output tokens *of its own*
- CLI's `result.usage` (cumulative): 2800 input / 120 output tokens

| | input | output |
|---|---|---|
| **Expected** `finish-step` #2 usage | 1800 | 70 |
| **Actual** `finish-step` #2 usage | 2800 | 120 |

## Why it matters

Anything consuming `finish-step`/`finish` to answer "how many tokens did the
model just use" — most obviously, a live "how full is the context window
right now" indicator — overcounts by the sum of every prior step in the turn,
on every ordinary multi-tool-call turn. It's easy to miss in testing because
a single-model-call turn (no tools, or the harness's built-in tools handled
in one shot) never shows a discrepancy: cumulative-so-far and "this step's
usage" are numerically identical when there's only one step.

This is a different bug from #18618 (subagent `Task`-tool activity bleeding
into the parent step's usage) — that one is fixed as of
`harness-claude-code@1.0.70`. This one reproduces unchanged against the
latest published version as of this writing
(`@ai-sdk/harness-claude-code@1.0.78`, see `package.json`).

## What this reproduction does

`repro.ts` imports the package's actual shipped bridge source (by relative
filesystem path into `node_modules`, since the package's `exports` map only
publishes the top-level entry point — the npm tarball does ship the `src/`
directory, pinned to whatever version is installed) and feeds it a
protocol-accurate two-step Claude Code CLI `stream-json` sequence: one Bash
tool round trip, then a final text answer, then the terminal `result`
message. It asserts the second `finish-step`'s usage equals that step's own
usage. It currently fails (exit code 1) — that's the bug. If/when this is
fixed upstream, it should print `PASS` and exit 0.
